checks: Exact CLI identity, policy, phase and pair validation precede native open; module reads are bounded to 16 bytes through 16 MiB.
Actual output words are compared before close; submit, wait, comparison, explicit close and success checks precede the end timestamp.
Trace/output retention, reset of the already closed operation and serialization occur after the primary timer; post-reset counts catch native cleanup deferred beyond close.
One context and 33 serial closed operations use the fixed fixture and alternating poison; failed batches stop without resubmission.
The observer scans exactly three live slots, has scalar counts, forwards native calls and performs no native query, output or heap allocation in tensor-buffer wrappers.
Open/release and post-prime/post-batch snapshots query live native state outside primary intervals; disabled counters remain unqueried/unreturned.
Same source and Makefile compile both policy arms into one binary per format; the CLI policy enum selects the existing runtime implementation.
The runtime, runtime API and native matmul kernel have no diff from base HEAD in this review.
limitations: Review is limited to the four named source files and their API use; full runner/archive/workflow enforcement is independently reviewed elsewhere.
Host synthetic tests do not prove native tensor arithmetic or speedup.
The 320-byte figure is requested tensor payload, not device-wide allocator overhead, host RSS or physical reclamation.

observations.subject: A rejected operation is serialized and a failure marker is flushed before operation.reset() when bounded close returns. The existing destructor drains indefinitely. Each requested wait/close timeout is 120 seconds; the external runner caps the entire process at 180 seconds. A persistently blocking wait plus close may be killed before a native failure prefix, so the supervised timeout receipt is the failure evidence in that case.

Failed native releases remain errors. Zero observer bookkeeping after a failed release is not proof of native or physical memory reclamation; successful output requires zero errors and complete cleanup results.
